name: Xavier Becerra
title: Democratic nominee for Governor of California (2026); former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services
years_of_service: California State Assembly 1990 to 1992; U.S. House 1993 to 2017; California Attorney General January 2017 to March 2021; U.S. HHS Secretary March 2021 to January 2025. (Wikipedia)
background: Becerra was born January 26, 1958, in Sacramento. He earned a B.A. in economics from Stanford in 1980 and a J.D. from Stanford Law School in 1984. He worked for state Senator Art Torres and as a deputy attorney general under John Van de Kamp before winning an Assembly seat in 1990. (Wikipedia)

He represented Los Angeles in the U.S. House for 24 years (1993 to 2017), rising to chair the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (1997 to 1999) and the House Democratic Caucus (2013 to 2017). Gov. Jerry Brown appointed him Attorney General in January 2017, making him the state's first Latino AG; he won a full term in 2018 with 63%. As AG he filed more than 120 lawsuits against the first Trump administration, including leading a 21-state coalition defending DACA and leading the multistate defense of the Affordable Care Act that the Supreme Court upheld. (Wikipedia; CalMatters)

The Senate confirmed him 50 to 49 as HHS Secretary in March 2021. His tenure included the first Medicare drug-price negotiations (10 drugs, with discounts of 38% to 79%) and an overhaul of the organ-transplant network. He was criticized for low visibility during the pandemic and over the Office of Refugee Resettlement, which lost contact with about 85,000 unaccompanied migrant children over two years. (Wikipedia; CalMatters)

He declared for governor on April 2, 2025, and placed first in the June 2, 2026 primary with 27.98%. In November 2025 Politico reported that aides, including his longtime chief of staff, had siphoned about $225,000 from his dormant campaign accounts over two years. Becerra was not accused of wrongdoing but was criticized for not noticing until federal investigators contacted him. (Wikipedia)

endorsements_received.name: Tom Steyer
endorsements_received.notes: Endorsed Becerra after finishing third in the June primary (CalMatters).
